frames.poseDescription: Beginning of the casting action, a subtle inhale and focused gaze. Knees only barely flex; qin remains at the idle angle. Anatomical right fingers curl inward just above the central strings, with the right elbow beginning to lift. Anatomical left hand maintains firm upper-qin support. This is an active musical preparation, with a small forward chin tuck and slight shoulder engagement.

Right elbow rises about 8 degrees from the preceding initial inhale, lifting the right wrist one finger-width off the strings. Chin lowers slightly toward the qin and knees soften about 2 degrees. Left hand draws the upper qin a little closer to the chest without changing its rigid shape. Ribbons are still nearly resting.

Right forearm rotates inward and right fingertips make a small preparatory sweep over the lower strings. Left wrist tilts the whole rigid qin upward 3 degrees from its idle angle. Shoulders begin a tiny backward windup and eyes stay toward the opponent. The near sleeve begins to drape outward, while hair stays nearly at rest.

The first preparatory pluck completes: right wrist flexes down near the lower string edge and elbow opens away from the waist. Qin is now 5 degrees above idle. Knees flex gently and torso leans 2 degrees backward into the musical windup. Left support remains at the upper qin. Ribbon ends begin a small trailing curve.

Gathering phase begins. Right hand lifts back up from the preparatory pluck toward upper-middle strings, fingers held softly together. Right elbow travels upward and backward; torso leans 4 degrees back with the chin lifted slightly. Left hand raises the whole qin to 7 degrees above idle; grounded feet remain planted. Sleeves trail the rising forearm.

Gathering grows: the right wrist moves farther back toward the torso and above the string plane, forearm angled up with delicate curved fingers. Right shoulder draws back another small increment, knees flex about 5 degrees, and qin reaches 8 degrees above idle. Ribbons continue to lag gently backward; no magical glow or particles appear.

Near the apex of preparation, torso comes closer to upright while the right elbow stays raised. Right wrist draws to the farthest windup point, just behind the middle string plane, fingers poised for one decisive sweep. Knees bend a little deeper and left support presents the qin 9 degrees above idle. Hair and sleeves curve opposite the imminent forward movement.

One moment before release. Weight loads through planted legs, torso inclines 3 degrees forward, right elbow begins driving the forearm down and outward, and curved right fingers hover immediately above the middle strings before contact. Left hand locks the upper qin at 10 degrees above idle. Her eyes focus firmly on the opponent; trailing ribbons remain behind the torso.

Release key pose: front knee bent gently, torso inclined 7 degrees forward, anatomical LEFT hand firmly supporting the upper section of the one rigid long qin, anatomical RIGHT hand has just swept forcefully across the middle strings toward the opponent. Right wrist extends and fingers open delicately a little beyond the near string edge. Focused violet eyes and a slightly open determined mouth. Qin is 10 degrees above idle. Sleeves and pale-lavender translucent ribbons trail backward in one smooth arc.

Immediate follow-through after the release. Torso inclines 8 degrees forward, right forearm travels a little farther down and outward beyond the near string edge, right fingers now more relaxed and separated. Right elbow begins lowering while left support keeps qin at 9 degrees above idle. Knees absorb the motion; the leading sleeve is at its widest delayed extension and ribbon ends continue trailing.

Recovery starts. Torso eases back to a 6-degree forward lean, right wrist turns inward and the open hand rises back toward the lower-middle strings. Right elbow drops nearer the ribcage. Left support lowers the whole qin to 7 degrees above idle without bending it. Hair tips still trail the release but the sleeve starts folding back.

Torso returns to a 4-degree forward lean as knees begin straightening. Right fingers curl again and pass just above the middle strings on the return path, elbow now halfway down toward idle. Qin lowers to 5 degrees above idle. Left hand stays on the same upper section. Ribbon ends reverse their delayed sway with a small soft curve.

The hand returns over the qin: right fingertips hover a finger-width above their original central plucking position and wrist straightens. Torso is only 2 degrees forward, knees nearly restored, and qin lowers to 3 degrees above idle. Facial effort softens to alert concentration. Near sleeve folds inward while the lower ribbon retains a last delayed oscillation.

Settling phase. Torso is nearly upright, qin only 2 degrees above idle. Right index and middle fingers gently approach the central strings to mute the final imaginary note, with a small remaining elbow bend. Left support steadies the upper qin. Knees finish extending softly; hair and ribbons retain a slight natural backward curve.

Almost settled: right fingertips lightly contact the middle strings, right wrist relaxes a small angle toward the body and elbow lowers a final increment. Qin returns to 1 degree above idle. Shoulders relax but eyes remain watchful toward the opponent. Sleeve and ribbons visibly fall closer to their resting curves while boots stay planted.

Final alert settling pose, ready to connect back to idle. Qin returns exactly to the resting angle and left hand holds the same upper section. Right fingers release the gentle string mute and hover just above the middle strings, wrist a little raised compared with frame15. Torso is upright with relaxed knees and calm focused face. Sleeve reaches rest while the last ribbon tip remains slightly displaced from idle. This is a freshly drawn final action pose, never a copied idle image.
